theorems.label: thm:certificate-soundness
theorems.text: [Finite certificate soundness] \label{thm:certificate-soundness} Suppose the standalone verifier accepts a positive certificate for an admitted instance. Then the certificate lists exactly the rooted reachable graph; every edge strictly lowers \(\measure\); every reachable local peak is joinable; the rooted relation is confluent; and the recomputed Boolean semantic fields are correct for the residual grammar.

[One-slot terminal outcomes] Every maximal execution ends with fact \(x^*\). Its output is either empty, when emission can remain disabled along a maximal analysis schedule and at \(x^*\), or equals \(E(y)\) for some reachable fact \(y\in R\) with \(g(y)\). Conversely, each guard-enabled reachable fact can be used for immediate emission and then followed by analysis to \(x^*\).

theorems.label: thm:newman
theorems.text: [Reachable Newman criterion] \label{thm:newman} For an admitted rooted system, the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item every reachable local peak is joinable; \item the full relation is confluent on reachable states; and \item every reachable state has exactly one reachable normal form. \end{enumerate}

theorems.label: lem:persistence
theorems.text: [Persistence along source analysis] \label{lem:persistence} Under GP, if \(g_r(x)\) and \((p,x)\astep^{*}(p,y)\), then \(g_r(y)\). In particular, \(g_r(\closure p(x))\).

theorems.label: lem:mixed-commute
theorems.text: [Normalized mixed-step commutation] \label{lem:mixed-commute} Assume GP and CC. If \((p,x)\astep(p,y)\) and rewrite \(r:p\to q\) is enabled at \(x\), then it is enabled at \(y\) and \[ \closure q(\tau_r(x))=\closure q(\tau_r(y)). \]

theorems.label: lem:normalization-simulation
theorems.text: [Normalization simulation] \label{lem:normalization-simulation} Assume GP and CC. Every full execution projects to a saturated execution after deleting analysis steps and normalizing after each rewrite. In particular, if \((p,x)\) is full-reachable, then \((p,\closure p(x))\) is saturated-reachable.

theorems.label: lem:saturated-confluence
theorems.text: [Saturated termination and confluence] \label{lem:saturated-confluence} The saturated relation terminates. Under SLC, it is confluent on its reachable states.

theorems.label: thm:modular
theorems.text: [Modular saturation] \label{thm:modular} If GP, CC, and SLC hold, then the full rooted staged transition system is state-confluent.

theorems.label: prop:not-necessary
theorems.text: [The modular criterion is not necessary] \label{prop:not-necessary} There exists an admitted confluent system that fails GP.

theorems.label: prop:program-criterion
theorems.text: [Exact program criterion] \label{prop:program-criterion} The root has a schedule-independent residual program exactly when \[ \left|\{\pi_P(t)\mid t\in\NF(s_0)\}\right|=1. \] State confluence implies this property, but the converse fails.

theorems.label: thm:pathwise-preservation
theorems.text: [Pathwise preservation] \label{thm:pathwise-preservation} If every rewrite used along a rooted execution is observationally preserving, then every program on that execution has the same denotation as the initial program.

theorems.label: cor:deterministic-preservation
theorems.text: [Deterministic source-equivalent residual] \label{cor:deterministic-preservation} If all reachable rewrites preserve observation and the root has a schedule-independent residual program, then that unique residual program is observationally equivalent to the source. The premise on schedule independence may be supplied by Theorem~\ref{thm:modular} or by the exact program criterion.

theorems.label: lem:coheight
theorems.text: [Strict growth lowers coheight] \label{lem:coheight} If \(x\sqsubset y\), then \(h(y)<h(x)\).

theorems.label: lem:measure
theorems.text: [Every full step lowers the measure] \label{lem:measure} If \(s\step t\), then \(\measure(t)<\measure(s)\).

theorems.label: thm:termination
theorems.text: [Termination] \label{thm:termination} Every execution in an admitted finite staged system is finite. The reachable graph is acyclic, and every reachable state reaches at least one normal state.

theorems.label: lem:least-closure
theorems.text: [Least common closure] \label{lem:least-closure} For every program \(p\) and fact \(x\), every fair analysis-only execution from \(x\) terminates at the same fact \(\closure p(x)\). This fact is the least common fixed point above \(x\).

theorems.label: lem:closure-laws
theorems.text: [Closure laws] \label{lem:closure-laws} For every \(p\), \(\closure p\) is extensive, monotone, and idempotent. If \((p,x)\astep(p,y)\), then \(\closure p(x)=\closure p(y)\).

theorems.label: cor:analysis-peaks
theorems.text: [Analysis peaks join] \label{cor:analysis-peaks} Every local analysis/analysis peak from \((p,x)\) joins at \((p,\closure p(x))\).

theorems_without_nearby_proof.label: cor:deterministic-preservation
theorems_without_nearby_proof.text: [Deterministic source-equivalent residual] \label{cor:deterministic-preservation} If all reachable rewrites preserve observation and the root has a schedule-independent residual program, then that unique residual program is observationally equivalent to the source. The premise on schedule independence may be supplied by Theorem~\ref{thm:modular} or by the exact program criterion.
